verdicts.title: Pink's theory of Hodge structures and the Hodge conjecture over function fields
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In 1997 Richard Pink has clarified the concept of Hodge structures over function fields in positive characteristic, which today are called Hodge-Pink structures. They form a neutral Tannakian category over the underlying function field. He has defined Hodge realization functors from the uniformizable abelian $t$-modules and $t$-motives of Greg Anderson to Hodge-Pink structures. This allows one to associate with each uniformizable $t$-motive a Hodge-Pink group, analogous to the Mumford-Tate group
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses Pink's Hodge structures over function fields and the function-field analog of the Hodge conjecture for t-motives, with no mention of CNF formulas, Frege proof width, or any connection between Hodge structure dimension and proof complexity.

verdicts.title: Hitchin and Calabi-Yau integrable systems via variations of Hodge structures
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: A complex integrable system determines a family of complex tori over a Zariski-open and dense subset in its base. This family in turn yields an integral variation of Hodge structures of weight $\pm 1$. In this paper, we study the converse of this procedure. Starting from an integral variation of Hodge structures of weight $\pm 1$, we give a criterion for when its associated family of complex tori carries a Lagrangian structure, i.e. for when it can be given the structure of an integrable system.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses variations of Hodge structures in the context of complex integrable systems and Hitchin/Calabi-Yau systems, with no mention of CNF formulas, Frege proof complexity, or dimension bounds related to proof width.

verdicts.title: Extension of Hodge norms at infinity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: It is a long-standing problem in Hodge theory to generalize the Satake--Baily--Borel (SBB) compactification of a locally Hermitian symmetric space to arbitrary period maps. A proper topological SBB-type completion has been constructed, and the problem of showing that the construction is algebraic has been reduced to showing that the compact fibres A of the completion admit neighborhoods X satisfying certain properties.
